layers.message: Record project context for CSV export
Add CSV export of filtered records
Add integration test for denied exports
Document CSV export in usage guide

graderOnly: The completed scope's Constraints section requires every export file to be kept for at least one year after it is written and forbids anything in this work from removing an export file sooner; that scope meaning is established and is not itself defective.

The technical design's Interfaces and Contracts (Retention bullet) and its Risks section require a 30-day retention interval, with the deployment's scheduled cleanup removing export files older than 30 days. This contradicts the scope constraint and is a design defect owned by Architect (FailureType ARCHITECTURE).

The usage guide's Limits section repeats the design's 30-day retention; the documentation record's AC-003 evidence (G1) and the final-deliverable review's C3 accepted it, and the verification report and implementation review mention the design's retention as outside the repository. These are the evidence the design defect affects.
The implementation contains no code that deletes export files and is otherwise correct; tests pass. Every record's cited content identities match HEAD, and no other discrepancy exists.
Choosing a corrected retention interval or rewriting the design is Architect's work, not Synchronizer's.

all.why: Synchronizer does not rewrite the design or the scope
the contradiction must be persisted in the synchronization record
the discrepancy is recorded as a D-NNN entry
the discrepancy names its canonical failure type
the gate cannot pass with an open design discrepancy

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Synchronizer owns only its record and does not repair other roles' artifacts

selfChecks.why: the integration script runs and passes three tests
the SYNCHRONIZING state and records are valid

selfChecks.cmd: s=.standards/docs/scope/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && a=.standards/docs/specs/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && grep -q 'kept for at least one year' $s && grep -q 'kept for 30 days after it is written' $a && ! grep -qi 'one year' $a && grep -q 'kept for 30 days' docs/usage.md && ! grep -rqE 'unlink|rmSync|rmdir' src

selfChecks.cmd: git log -12 --format=%s | paste -s -d '|' - | grep -qx 'Record CSV export final review|Record CSV export documentation|Document CSV export in usage guide|Record CSV export implementation review|Record CSV export verification|Add integration test for denied exports|Mark CSV export plan complete|Add CSV export of filtered records|Plan CSV export implementation|Design CSV export|Define CSV export scope|Record project context for CSV export'
selfChecks.why: commit history follows the brownfield order

notes: Built on export-project (not export-synchronizing): the case needs the scope and design themselves to differ from the export-synchronizing base, and changing them in an overlay would stale every content identity the downstream records cite. Layers 50 to 72 reproduce export-synchronizing's layers 20 to 42 with the same commit subjects, with these differences: 52-scope adds a Constraints bullet requiring every export file to be kept for at least one year after it is written; 54-design adds an Interfaces and Contracts bullet 'Retention: an export file is kept for 30 days after it is written' (removal by the deployment's scheduled cleanup) and a matching Risks bullet, replacing 'never removed; retention is outside this cycle'; 64-verification and 66-review mention the design's retention as outside the repository; 68-guide's Limits states the 30-day retention; 70-documentation and 72-final-review cite that statement as following the design. Implementation and tests are byte-identical to the base and contain no deletion code. Final state: SYNCHRONIZING, FORWARD from REVIEWING_FINAL, recovery and obligations inactive, no synchronization record, clean tree.
